reason: Not a trap: the line ends about level (dxc6 is the engine's first choice) with nothing won, and …Qxc3+ is their engine's first choice, not a slip. It is your own gambit at your third move (b4 instead of Bb5, costs 0.83, about one master game in a thousand) with its own plan: d4 for the c-pawn, c4 and Nxc3 with tempo on the queen, Rb1 offering the knight, Bd2 and d5 winning the piece back; taught honestly as a gambit, about level at the end.
